Q: ERROR : S_BROM_DOWNLOAD_DA_FAIL (0x7D4) A:

SP flash tool BROM Error :- S_BROM_DOWNLOAD_DA_FAIL

Fail to download DA to baseband chip's internal SRAM!

Reason

  1. There’s a cable communication problem between Flash Tool and Boot ROM.

  2. Target might be shutdown unexpectedly or target lost power supply.

  3. The DA is not correct.

Solution

  1. Try again.

  2. Proceed H/W checking in download cable and target side com port.

  3. Monitor if power-drop occurred on the target side.

Find details and the Latest Tool - sp flash tool

Q: Jenkins git fetch returned status code 143 A:

I found a solution. Running Jenkins as a service with systemctl resolved the problem, instead of running Jenkins with java -jar jenkins.war.

To give more details: According to the documentation, Jenkins is started by

java -jar jenkins.war

And it was visible as running in the system when I checked it with:

ps aux | grep jenkins

However, on CentOS 7 the suggested way of running Jenkins is to run it as a daemon with systemctl command. When I checked it with

sudo systemctl status jenkins.service

it was inactive. So I started Jenkins with

sudo systemctl start jenkins.service

and it worked.

Q: pygsheets - Load credentials from dict instead of file A:

You can authenticate with a string instead of a file. For example:

import pygsheets
gc = pygsheets.authorize(service_account_json=json.dumps(secret))

Q: How do I display strings and variables on the same line? It's more than just numbers A:

You can use the to_string() function to convert a number to a string.

Disp "HI"+to_string(5) outputs HI5.

In your code, you can replace:

Disp "B: ",B
Disp "LA: ",L
Disp "SA: ",S

with:

Disp "B: "+to_string(B)
Disp "LA: "+to_string(L)
Disp "SA: "+to_string(S)

Q: Create a foreign key in SQL using a subset of values from a primary key column A:

Declare employee trigger

From what I understand, using triggers is the standard way to achieve the goal:

-- declare tables

CREATE TABLE Company (
    Company_ID   INT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
    Company_Name VARCHAR(40),
    Can_Employ   BIT NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE Employee (
    Employee_ID   INT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
    Employee_Name VARCHAR(40),
    Employer      INT NOT NULL FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES Company(Company_ID)
);

GO -- this is added because "CREATE TRIGGER" must be the only statement in the batch

-- declare the trigger

CREATE TRIGGER Employee_Insert_Or_Update ON Employee
AFTER INSERT, UPDATE
AS BEGIN
    IF EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM   inserted AS i
        JOIN   Company  AS c ON i.Employer = c.Company_ID
        WHERE  c.Can_Employ = 0
    )
    BEGIN
        RAISERROR ('Employer cannot hire employees', 11, 1);
        ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;
    END
END;
GO

Note that the extra GO keyword inserted in the middle of code seems out of place, but it is actually needed. When using SQL Server Management Studio, GO keyword marks the end of a batch. But creating a new trigger must be done in a single batch, hence it's needed before CREATE TRIGGER.

Choosing severity level 11 when raising the error is common practice for a user level error, the range of this severities category is 11~16. The error state value 1 is just arbitrary.

See also:

  • RAISERROR: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/language-elements/raiserror-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17
  • Levels of severity: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/errors-events/database-engine-error-severities?view=sql-server-ver17

Optionally declare company trigger

That trigger only ensures adding / updating employee records is guarded against the case when Can_Employ column of company table is 0. It will not block from updating existing company data from replacing that column from 1 to 0.

If the requirement allows that, which means companies which still have employees can stop employing new employees, then one trigger on employee table is enough. Otherwise, a new trigger is needed for company table:

CREATE TRIGGER Company_Update ON Company
AFTER UPDATE
AS BEGIN
    IF EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM   inserted AS i
        JOIN   deleted  AS d ON i.Company_ID = d.Company_ID
        WHERE  d.Can_Employ = 1 AND i.Can_Employ = 0
    )
    BEGIN
        RAISERROR ('Cannot change Can_Employ from 1 to 0', 11, 2);
        ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;
    END
END;
GO

The inserted and deleted tables are "logical" tables which denote the data being inserted and the one being removed, respectively. See also:

  • Create trigger: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/create-trigger-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17
  • Use the inserted and deleted tables: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/triggers/use-the-inserted-and-deleted-tables?view=sql-server-ver17

Q: Access violation reading location 0x00000014. Using Streams A:

There's nothing wrong with the shown code.

What all those websites you've read have not fully explained to you is just because a C++ program crashes on a particular line does not mean that's where the bug is. I can easily come up with a minimum example that strcpy()s past the end of the array, corrupting the stack, then proceeds to do a bunch of work, and only crashing when an attempt is made to return from the function. There's nothing wrong with the return statement in C++, yet the code will crash at that point.

And there's nothing wrong with your getline() call either, or how it's used.

A programming error or a bug typically results in corrupted memory, but after stomping all over the memory, the code might not immediately attempt to use it, in any meaningful way, but proceeds on its way. At some pointer later, the program goes back and attempts to use its data structures, encounters garbage, and crashes.

The most likely explanation is that a bug that happened earlier ended up scribbling all over your std::ifstream, and/or name std::string. Now, you get around to calling getline() to read from the stream into this string, and the code blows up. Or, perhaps, something screwed up a pointer to an instance of this Author class. An attempt is made to execute this class method. The code blows up because the name class member is, obviously, utter junk. The bug would not be here, of course, but wherever the pointer to this Author class got screwed up.

The only way you can get help with your problem would be if you post a minimum, complete, and verifiable example that anyone can compile, execute, and reproduce your bug (pay attention to the "minimum" requirement, that doesn't mean that you get to post your entire code).

You will need to investigate the rest of your entire program, looking for your bug. Welcome to C++.

Q: Create a new file in the directory of the open file in Vim A:

If you're in the explorer view, you can create a file within the current directory with `%`

Then vim will prompt you to enter a file name. For what it's worth I'm running vim through iTerm
